{{short description|Israeli academic and physicist}}
'''Abraham Katzir''' ({{langx|he|אברהם קציר}}; born 1941 in [[Jerusalem]], [[Israel]]) is a [[Professor]] of [[Physics]] at [[Tel Aviv University]], holding the Carol and Mel Taub Chair in Applied Medical Physics.<ref>{{cite web|title=Applied Physics Group|url=http://www.tau.ac.il/~applphys|access-date=2012-07-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010106091600/http://www.tau.ac.il/~applphys/|archive-date=2001-01-06|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Abraham Katzir |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=UsRkna4AAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>  He is the son of Professor [[Aharon Katzir]], also a scientist, who was killed in 1972 in [[Ben-Gurion Airport]] by Japanese terrorists. His uncle, Professor [[Ephraim Katzir]], was the [[President of Israel]].

Abraham Katzir got his [[PhD]] from the [[Hebrew University]] in Jerusalem in 1974, and joined [[Caltech]] in [[Pasadena, California]], as a Senior [[Research Fellow]].  In 1977 he established the Applied Physics Group at [[Tel Aviv University]], which he heads.  In the past, Prof. Katzir worked in some of the top research laboratories in the US.  He was a Visiting Member of Staff  at AT&T [[Bell Laboratories]] in [[Summit, New Jersey]], and he was a visiting professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], and in [[Boston University]], [[Boston, Massachusetts]].

Katzir is an expert in the fields of biomedical [[optics]] and [[fiber optics]].  His group at [[Tel Aviv University]] developed special [[fibers]] made of crystalline [[silver halide]]s, which are among the few that are highly transparent in the middle-[[infrared]] (mid-IR).  He and members of the group have been involved with research and development of new methods and new systems, based on these fibers. They made significant contributions to the use of mid-IR fibers for scientific, medical, industrial and environmental protection applications.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Future of Suture|url=http://www.technologyreview.com/news/411212/healing-with-laser-heat/|publisher=MIT Technical Review}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Monitoring Water Through A Snake's Eyes|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2009/05/090512193241.htm|publisher=Science Daily}}</ref> In the course of this work, Katzir collaborated with leading scientists in major national laboratories, universities, research institutions and industrial companies, all over the world.{{citation needed|date=August 2012}}

Katzir supervised the research work of 100 students in [[MSc]] and [[PhD]] [[dissertations]] and their research was published in 400 scientific papers. He also published the book "Lasers and Optical Fibers in Medicine".<ref>{{cite book|last=Katzir|first=Abraham|title=Lasers and Optical Fibers in Medicine|year=1993|publisher=Academic Press}}</ref>

Katzir is the Chair of ILEOS,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Siegel-Itzkovich |first=Judy |date=2021-04-18 |title=New Israeli development is expected to revolutionize the field of skin cancer diagnosis |url=https://israel365news.com/345043/new-israeli-development-is-expected-to-revolutionize-the-field-of-skin-cancer-diagnosis/ |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=Israel365 News |language=en-US}}</ref> the Israel [[Lasers]] and Electro Optics Society,  and the Chair of the bi-annual '''OASIS''' (Optical Applied Science in Israel)  international conferences<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oasis6.org.il/scientific-program/|title=Organizing Committee {{!}} OASIS6 Conference|website=oasis6.org.il|access-date=2016-11-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161110042430/http://oasis6.org.il/scientific-program/|archive-date=2016-11-10|url-status=dead}}</ref> that this society organizes in Israel. He has been a member of the [[board of governors]] of [[SPIE]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=SPIE Directors' Award |url=https://spie.org/about-spie/spie-awards/spie-directors-award |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=spie.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=News Item |url=https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~bodek/dept/OSAsummary.html |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=www.pas.rochester.edu}}</ref>  the International Society for Optics and [[Photonics]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-06-06 |title=TAU develops revolutionary technique to 'solder' newly transplanted corneas |url=https://www.jpost.com/business-and-innovation/health-and-science/tau-develops-revolutionary-technique-to-solder-newly-transplanted-corneas-405224 |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en |issn=0792-822X}}</ref> a member of the board of [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|IUPAP]],{{citation needed|date=August 2012}}  the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]],{{citation needed|date=August 2012}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Abraham Katzir {{!}} 9th International Symposium on Sensor Science |url=https://sciprofiles.com/profile/1011054 |website=sciforum.net}}</ref>  and of other international bodies.  He has organized and chaired tens of international symposia and conferences in the fields of biomedical optics, optical fibers, and electro-optics.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=April 15, 2001 |title=IR-biosensor: flat silver halide fiber for bio-medical sensing? |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925400500007097 |journal= }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=December 12, 2004 |title=European Symposium on Optics and Photonics for Defence and Security |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234902414}}</ref>

Each year, Katzir organizes a series of popular lectures, called "In the [[Crucible]] of [[Revolution]]", in memory of his late father. Tens of thousands of people have attended these lectures.{{citation needed|date=August 2012}}
